test_title: PYST 22: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - English Language (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

“Though the facts were evident, the jury chose to ignore them,” he observed.

options.text: He observed the facts had been evident, but jury ignored them.
He observed that though the facts had been evident, the jury had chosen to ignore them.
He observed though facts were evident, jury ignored it.
He observed that even though facts were code evident, jury ignored them.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He observed that though the facts had been evident, the jury had chosen to ignore them.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb in Past Tense:**
 
 
• The reporting verb **"observed"** is in the past tense. When the reporting verb is in the past, the tenses within the reported speech must undergo **backshifting** (moving one step back into the past).
 
 
 
• **Tense Changes (Backshifting):**
 
 
• The simple past **"were"** changes to the past perfect **"had been"**.
 
• The simple past **"chose"** changes to the past perfect **"had chosen"**.
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is used to connect the reporting clause with the reported speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks and the comma separating the reporting verb are removed.
 
• The sentence structure maintains the subordinating conjunction **"though"** to preserve the original meaning.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He observed that though the facts had been evident, the jury had chosen to ignore them."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He observed the facts had been evident, but jury ignored them." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the conjunction from **"though"** to **"but"** and fails to backshift **"ignored"**. It also lacks the necessary article "the" before "jury".
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He observed though facts were evident, jury ignored it." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it lacks tense backshifting, misses articles, and uses the singular pronoun **"it"** to refer to the plural "facts".
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He observed that even though facts were code evident, jury ignored them." 
 
 
• Incorrect due to the nonsensical phrase **"code evident"** (a likely typo), missing articles, and a lack of proper tense backshifting.
